messages:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: alert: sustained throttle events detected on inference-pool-eu-central. queue_depth > 2500 for 3m, tokens/sec spike. auto-scale attempted +2 nodes but still >80% token throttle rate. Links: https://dash.redwood/alerts/1829001122
Alex C: I'm on it. popping into the pool to check backlog and recent deploys.
Jordan (on-call): saw a brief deploy 45m ago from eng-runtime — did that touch routing?
Lee: Not to routing. small kernel fallback change, should be safe. will check logs.
Maria S: Customer impact: a few high-traffic tenants reporting 5xx and streaming drops. Support ticket count up 4 in last 10m.
Tess (product): Which tenants? need heads-up to CS.
Alex C: tenant ids: acct-732, acct-19, acct-444. acct-732 gets a lot of long-context calls -> KV hit ratio high.
Jordan (on-call): running a quick query on tokens/sec per tenant: ```SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) FROM requests WHERE ts > now()-5m GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sum(tokens) DESC LIMIT 10;```
Jordan (on-call): result: acct-732 ~ 4.8M tokens/5m, acct-19 ~1.2M, acct-444 ~900k.
Lee: queue depth tailing on shard 7. log snippet: ```shard=7 queue_depth=2982 active_workers=32 throttle_rate=0.82```
Alex C: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase max_nodes for pool to +4 (manual override) 2) enable tenant soft-throttle for non-critical tenants 3) route acct-732 to a smaller model variant to reduce tokens.
Maria S: agree. I'll notify CS about acct-732 routing change.
Jordan (on-call): doing #1 now: `infractl pool update --pool inference-pool-eu-central --max-nodes 64` -> submitted.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: cluster-scaler started scale up to 4 nodes (eta ~3m).
Alex C: while that comes up, applying tenant soft-throttle for acct-444 and acct-19: `admin throttle set --tenant acct-444 --p50 0.8 --reason "surge mitigation"`
Lee: applying route change for acct-732 to model:redwood-small-v1 with knob reduce_max_len=2048.```route update acct-732 --model redwood-small-v1 --param max_len=2048```
Tess (product): we should also consider a post-mortem on why long-context tenants caused cascade. tagging product and solutions.
Jordan (on-call): scale up completed. new nodes healthy. queue depth dropping: shard=7 queue_depth=420 active_workers=48 throttle_rate=0.12
Alex C: p99 latency back to normal for most routes, still seeing a few streaming dropouts.
Maria S: CS confirms fewer tickets after routing change. one remaining ticket from acct-732 edge case.
Lee: capturing perf profile. I see increased KV cache misses during the tail of that traffic which amplified token usage.
Alex C: root cause hypothesis: concentrated long-context workload + changed kernel fallback earlier increased per-token CPU causing slower processing -> queue accumulation -> autoscaler reaction too late.
Jordan (on-call): action items for post-incident: - add a tokens/sec per-tenant alert (agg over 5m) - adjust queue_depth alert to consider shard-level v global - add a suppression window for short spikes to avoid noisy pages - create dashboard widget for tenant-level throttle events.
Maria S: proposed thresholds: tokens/sec per-tenant > 700k for 3m -> page on-call. queue_depth per-shard > 1500 for 5m -> page. Keep global queue_depth as warning at 3000.
Lee: also propose a new synthetic test that simulates concentrated long-context traffic to evaluate autoscale latency.
Tess (product): prioritize tenant-level alert and dashboard. Customer comms: I'll draft a short note for affected customers mentioning routing fallback and mitigation steps.
Alex C: I'll file a runbook ticket with steps we just executed and add checklist: manual max_nodes override, tenant soft-throttle, model-fallback, and who to loop in. Assign to Jordan for follow-up.
Jordan (on-call): filed: https://tracker/INC-9834 "Surge signal bakeoff runbook + alerts" assigned -> Jordan. Added tags: post-incident, autoscale, alerts.
OpsBot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by Jordan (on-call).
Maria S: Proposed alert tuning summary to implement after cool-down (assign to eng-sre): 1) new metric tokens/sec per-tenant + page threshold, 2) shard-level queue depth alert, 3) 3m dedupe window for autoscale-triggered pages, 4) dashboard tile for throttle_rate by tenant.
Alex C: agreed. Also roll-forward: runtime team to review kernel fallback change for any perf regressions. Lee, please own that.
Lee: on it. will open PR to revert if repro.
Tess (product): thanks. I'll send the customer note once the runbook + mitigations are documented.
Jordan (on-call): closing live thread. leave follow-ups in tracker. :thumbsup:
